title_prefix: Fee estimator tracks every mempool entry
mechanism: BPE-NOTE-ENTRY (src/mempool/block-policy-estimator.lisp:554-560) takes only (txid fee vsize height) and BPE-PROCESS-TRANSACTION (:352-362) records the transaction in all three horizons with no predicate at all: there is no parameter through which Core's four exclusions could be expressed and no height comparison. Core's processTransaction (refs/bitcoin/src/policy/fees/block_policy_estimator.cpp:595-637) returns early when txHeight != nBestSeenHeight, then computes validForFeeEstimation = !m_mempool_limit_bypassed && !m_submitted_in_package && m_chainstate_is_current && m_has_no_mempool_parents and counts anything failing it in untrackedTxs. Those four flags are filled in at refs/bitcoin/src/validation.cpp:1304-1307 and 1408-1411 from args.m_bypass_limits, args.m_package_submission, IsCurrentForFeeEstimation(m_active_chainstate) and m_pool.HasNoInputsOf(tx). Our single drive site is ACCEPT-VALIDATED-TX (src/mempool/mempool.lisp:906-909), which is the shared tail of EVERY acceptance path, so each of Core's exclusions is fed straight in: reorg re-add with :bypass-limits t (src/validation/block.lisp:3021-3028), package submission (src/validation/packages.lisp:235-237), mempool.dat replay at startup (src/node/mempool-persist.lisp:111-114), and any child whose parents are still in the pool. Grepped: no IBD, chainstate-current or syncing test exists anywhere in src/mempool/block-policy-estimator.lisp or src/mempool/mempool.lisp.
consequence: The estimator learns from transactions whose confirmation time was bought by somebody else. A CPFP child teaches it that its own low feerate confirms in one block, which is exactly the inference the parent paid for, and the differential replay reproduces the finder's number: 1000 sat/kvB with children tracked against 20000 sat/kvB with Core's gate applied, a 20x underestimate, identical in economical and conservative mode at both targets tested. A wallet acting on that builds a transaction at 1/20 of the feerate the same history justifies, so it does not confirm. The reorg and mempool.dat cases push the same direction: a re-added or replayed transaction is recorded as if it had entered at the current tip, and Core drops all of them (nBestSeenHeight is 0 in a freshly constructed estimator, which is what a restart has). A wrong fee a client acts on: S2, not S1 - no funds are lost, the transaction simply sits.
evidence: (1) Probe ga11v-rpcutil-p4 (scratch, not committed) *GA11-HEIGHT-GATE*: a fresh estimator, one transaction announced at height 500 -> (:BEST-HEIGHT 0 :TX-HEIGHT 500 :TRACKED 1 :CORE-WOULD-TRACK 0). (2) *GA11-REPLAY-OURS* vs *GA11-REPLAY-CORE-GATE*, a 400-block synthetic replay, 20 parents/block at 20000 sat/kvB confirming in 3 blocks and 20 children/block at 1000 sat/kvB confirming in 1: ours (:T2-ECON 1000 :T2-CONS 1000 :T6-ECON 1000 :T6-CONS 1000), with the children withheld as Core withholds them (:T2-ECON 20000 :T2-CONS 20000 :T6-ECON 20000 :T6-CONS 20000). Same code path, same blocks, the only difference is the gate. (3) *GA11-CPFP-DRIVE* drives the REAL entry point rather than the estimator directly - two transactions through bl.mp:accept-validated-tx, the second spending the first: (:MEMPOOL-SIZE 2 :CHILD-HAS-MEMPOOL-PARENT 1 :TRACKED 2 :CORE-WOULD-TRACK 1), so the child with an in-mempool parent IS recorded by the shipped path. Ours: src/mempool/block-policy-estimator.lisp:352-362,554-560; src/mempool/mempool.lisp:884-911; src/validation/block.lisp:3021-3028; src/validation/packages.lisp:235-237; src/node/mempool-persist.lisp:111-114. Core at d3056bc: policy/fees/block_policy_estimator.cpp:595-637; validation.cpp:1304-1307,1408-1411; kernel/mempool_entry.h:173-199.
fix_shape: Give BPE-NOTE-ENTRY the same information Core's NewMempoolTransactionInfo carries and let the estimator decide, rather than deciding at the call sites. Add a VALID-FOR-FEE-ESTIMATION argument (or the four booleans) to ACCEPT-VALIDATED-TX and thread it from each caller exactly as Core threads it out of ATMPArgs: :bypass-limits from the reorg re-add, a package flag from %ACCEPT-INTO-MEMPOOL, a chainstate-current predicate mirroring IsCurrentForFeeEstimation, and a has-no-mempool-parents test which the entry already knows (mempool-entry-parents is populated by MAKE-ENTRY-FROM-TX). Then add Core's first gate inside BPE-PROCESS-TRANSACTION: return early when HEIGHT differs from BLOCK-POLICY-ESTIMATOR-BEST-HEIGHT, which alone drops the mempool.dat replay and the side-chain cases, and count the rejects the way Core counts untrackedTxs so the behaviour is observable. Keep the gate in the estimator, not in the callers, so a future acceptance path cannot silently opt out.
